title: Rome: if all were written, the Church would lose her privilege of secret mysteries
source_text: XXIX. Tertium argumentum Pontificii sumunt ab Ecclesiae dignitate. Nam, inquiunt, ut olim Judaei excellabant omnibus nationibus, quia credita erant illis eloquia Dei, ut dicit Paulus cap. 3. Epist. ad Rom. ita nunc praestat Ecclesia Christi omnibus sectis, quod ipsa sola noverit omnia mysteria verae religionis, & conscia sit secretorum sponsi. At, si omnia essent scripta, nullum esset Ecclesiae privilegium. Nam nihil minus scirent haeretici, & Judaei, & Pagani de mysteriis fidei nostrae, quam nos ipsi, atque antistites nostri.
pass_a_gloss: The Pontificians take a third argument from the dignity of the Church. For, they say, as once the Jews excelled all nations, because the oracles of God were entrusted to them, as Paul says in Romans chapter 3, so now the Church of Christ surpasses all sects, because she alone knows all the mysteries of true religion, and is conscious of the secrets of the bridegroom. But if all things were written, there would be no privilege of the Church. For heretics, and Jews, and Pagans would know nothing less concerning the mysteries of our faith than we ourselves, and our bishops.
pass_b_english: Romans 3: Jews held the oracles — so the church alone holds true religion's secrets.
If everything is written, that privilege vanishes.
Heretics, Jews, and pagans would know the mysteries as well as we and our bishops.
